question: Why did the engine that lifted Apollo astronauts off the Moon have no igniter?
answer: Because its propellants ignite on contact. A hydrazine blend and nitrogen tetroxide burst into flame the moment they meet, so the engine needed only valves to open; pressurised helium pushed them in, so it had no pumps either. With no backup, every part left out was one that could not fail. Both are toxic.
move: The most reliable part is the one that is not there.
reference: Kelly, Moon Lander: How We Developed the Apollo Lunar Module, Smithsonian Institution Press, 2001
